evidence: The indium precursor was maintained at 40 °C to obtain sufficient vapor pressure and dose amount, as previously reported. N2 gas was used as purging and carrier gases. The N2 gas flow rate of 50 sccm was controlled by a mass flow controller. An ALD growth sequence for the indium oxide layer involved exposure to In(CH3)3[CH3OCH2CH2NHtBu] precursor for 1 s with assistant mode, N2 purging for 10 s, exposure to H2O for 0.1 s, and N2 purging for 10 s.
